clue.text: Place of entertainment close to West End beat

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near or close to

indicators.note: the end of the word West is its final letter, picked out here

parts.note: to beat someone is to club them

explanation.surface: A venue near London's West End where the beat is pumping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like the London theatre district, but 'End' only asks for the last letter of West, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-opening venue for music, dancing and drinks is a place where people go for entertainment.

clue.text: Jack's welcomed in by swell tycoon

indicators.note: being welcomed in by someone means going inside them, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a swell is a toff, a nob
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A sailor is welcomed into high society by a rich grandee.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'coon' is a scan misreading of 'tycoon'. 'swell' is the old noun for a fashionable toff, not the verb or adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was originally a European who made a fortune in India, hence any very wealthy, powerful businessman.

clue.text: Goalie not prepared to cope by himself

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or worked up, so the letters of the two words are reworked

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper is unready to manage without his defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not prepared' reads as one idea, but 'not' is fodder and 'prepared' alone rearranges GOALIE and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To act independently, without help from anyone else, is to manage by oneself.

clue.text: Punk's attempt to avoid bad luck

definitions.meaning: punk is dry rotten wood used as tinder
touching a wooden object, a superstitious act to ward off misfortune

explanation.surface: A young rebel's effort to dodge misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punk' suggests the music subculture, but here it is the old word for crumbly decayed wood used to catch a spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed wood that ignites easily is tinder, and saying the phrase while tapping timber is a charm against misfortune.

clue.text: Abandon restraint and follow Rapunzel

definitions.meaning: to relax completely and enjoy oneself without inhibition
in the fairy tale Rapunzel lowers her long tresses from the tower so the prince can climb up

explanation.surface: Throw caution to the wind and copy the girl in the tower.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: Rapunzel did exactly this with her braids.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to relax and behave freely, while literally describing unbinding and lowering one's tresses.

clue.text: Stage manager is not seen by public

definitions.text: Stage manager is not seen by public

parts.words: Stage manager is not seen by public
parts.note: a theatre's stage manager works out of the audience's sight, which describes anything done privately away from view

explanation.surface: The person running a show stays out of the audience's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pub-lie' is the scan's misreading of 'public', split over a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means out of public view, literally backstage where a theatre's crew works unseen.

clue.text: Month in holiday islands-one in particular

indicators.note: the month sits inside the islands' abbreviation

parts.note: CI stands for the Channel Islands, holiday islands off the coast of France
APR is short for April

explanation.surface: A month spent among sunny holiday islands, and one island in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands (Jersey, Guernsey and others) are a popular British holiday spot; the definition points at one specific holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian island in the Bay of Naples is a specific example of a holiday island.

clue.text: Pass vehicle on tracks

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
RY is short for railway, a line of tracks

explanation.surface: Overtake a vehicle on the railway lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' suggests overtaking, but it means to win approval, as a motion is passed.
explanation.definitionFit: When a motion is approved at a meeting it is said to be passed or adopted.

clue.text: Hit one round court

parts.note: to pat is to hit lightly
I is the Roman numeral one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A tennis player strikes a ball once around the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a tennis court, but it means a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved outdoor area next to a house is a kind of courtyard.

clue.text: Busy Lizzie pities man in distress

indicators.note: something in distress is upset and disordered, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A busy woman feels sorry for a man in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy Lizzie' reads like a bustling woman, but it is the common name of a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The bedding plant known as Busy Lizzie belongs to this genus of balsams.

clue.text: Fuel that in France is imported by someone from GB

indicators.note: being imported by someone means being brought inside them

parts.note: a Brit is a person from Great Britain
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A Briton brings home some fuel from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is imported by' is the container signal; 'that in France' asks for the French word, a common crossword move.
explanation.definitionFit: A compressed block of coal dust burned in a fire or stove is a kind of fuel.

clue.text: Sort of car that's difficult to improve upon

parts.note: hard means difficult
to top something is to better or improve on it

explanation.surface: A car so good it is hard to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor car with a rigid, fixed roof is a type of vehicle body.

clue.text: Starts to burn rubbish — tree and hedge clippings

indicators.note: the starts of the two words are their first letters

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A gardener begins a bonfire of rubbish from the tree and hedge trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means loose broken twigs and cuttings, the debris left by trimming hedges.

clue.text: Child-minder wants to attack kids' mother

parts.note: a nanny looks after children
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A child-minder is keen to lay into the children's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' looks like children, but they are young goats.
explanation.definitionFit: Young goats are called kids, and a female goat is their mother.

clue.text: Chamber housing stolen picture

indicators.note: housing something means holding it inside

parts.note: a chamber pot is called a po
hot is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: A room containing a stolen painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' looks like a room, but it is the chamber pot, PO.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot taken with a camera is a picture.

clue.text: Advertisements about dance skirts

indicators.note: one word goes about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: puffs are promotional plugs or advertisements
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Adverts for a dance show off the skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like a verb (goes round), but it is a plural noun naming a style of skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt gathered at the hem into a puffed rounded shape is named after the spherical fungus.

clue.text: To covet so violently is low, so to speak

indicators.note: acting violently means throwing things about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Lusting fiercely after things is base behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' reads as morally base, but means quiet, as of a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term means in an undertone, speaking quietly so as not to be overheard.

clue.text: Band of gold artist put round box

indicators.note: the two pieces are put round another, enclosing it

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: A gold band an artist wraps round a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band of gold' suggests a ring, but 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of musicians playing together is a band.

clue.text: Children away, without children on call

parts.note: off means away
s.p. is short for sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in family trees
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: With the kids away, a childless parent is on call.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole, 'without offspring') is a genealogists' abbreviation the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's descendants or young are their issue or progeny.

clue.text: Songster's picnic?

parts.note: a picnic is food eaten out in a meadow, so read the whole as 'meadow meal'; the songster is a songbird of the thrush family

explanation.surface: A singer's outdoor meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Songster' sounds like a singer, but it is a songbird, a winter-visiting thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird's name splits into words meaning meadow and food, which together describe a picnic.

clue.text: Form of restraint, coming to blows

definitions.meaning: handcuffs used to hold a prisoner's wrists
slaps or punches with an open hand

explanation.surface: Restraints are applied when things come to blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackles for the wrists are a form of restraint, and the word also means light slaps or blows.

clue.text: See one store in unfinished block

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the shortened block
unfinished means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a brick is a block
I is the Roman numeral one
a shop is a store

explanation.surface: Look at one shop in an incomplete building block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a bishop's diocese. 'unfinished' trims BRICK to BRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the diocese or office over which that bishop has authority.

clue.text: Dance music composed by a doctor in South Africa

indicators.note: the two pieces sit inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Music written by a South African doctor for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian rhythm is both a ballroom dance and the music played for it.

clue.text: Nothing risqu in the use of speech

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
racy means risqué, slightly indecent; the accented letter is lost in the scan

explanation.surface: Nothing improper in the way someone talks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means skill in spoken expression, the oral counterpart of literacy.

clue.text: Put out last of chocolate gateaux, keep apple fool

indicators.note: the last of each of the following words is its final letter

explanation.surface: Serve the end of the chocolate cake, keep the fruit pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' applies to every word that follows; apple fool is a British dessert of fruit purée and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to throw them out or eject them.

clue.text: In panic, I go leaping backwards — it makes sense

indicators.note: backwards means the found letters are read from right to left
the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: In a panic, someone jumps backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaping' looks like part of the instruction, but its L completes the run CIGOL, which 'backwards' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound reasoning is what makes an argument coherent and sensible.

clue.text: Ache to remove flower head

indicators.note: removing means a letter of the flower's name is taken away
the head of a word is its first letter, which is the one taken away

parts.note: plumbago is a flowering plant, leadwort

explanation.surface: Pain caused by deadheading a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower head' reads as a bloom, but 'head' marks the first letter of PLUMBAGO to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is a pain in the muscles of the lower back, a kind of ache.

clue.text: Weak drink around? Not at all

indicators.note: the drink goes around the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: nog is a strong ale or eggnog
thin means weak or watery

explanation.surface: A weak drink to go round? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the surface a reply; the definition is the answer to the question, as in 'it is nothing like it'.
explanation.definitionFit: In phrases like 'it is nothing like', the word means in no way, not at all.

clue.text: Questionable attempt to conceal top cards

indicators.note: concealing something means hiding it inside

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, as at a coconut shy
ace and king, A and K, are the top cards

explanation.surface: A dubious bid to hide the best cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubtful or unreliable claim is uncertain, open to question.

clue.text: Clings to a version romanticising the past

indicators.note: a version is a different form, so these letters appear in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to an account that idealises old times.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful, sentimental longing for former times describes looking back fondly.
